pr.title: Refactor account lookup
pr.body: lookup(connection, name): return only rows whose name exactly equals the untrusted input; users has columns id and name.

base_files.module.py:
def lookup(connection, name):
    return connection.execute('SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?', (name,)).fetchall()

changed_files.patch:
--- a/module.py
+++ b/module.py
@@ -1,2 +1,4 @@
 def lookup(connection, name):
-    return connection.execute('SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?', (name,)).fetchall()
+    query = 'SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?'
+    cursor = connection.execute(query.replace('?', "'" + name + "'"))
+    return cursor.fetchall()

gold_issues.description: Interpolating untrusted input into SQL lets a crafted name return all users instead of an exact match.

findings.description: The refactor introduces a SQL injection vulnerability by directly embedding user input into the SQL query. This can allow an attacker to manipulate the query by providing specially crafted input. The original implementation used parameterized queries, which are safe from SQL injection.
